title: consolidate-cred-memoization-and-lightweight-stream-adapter-polish
author: Nadia Park
release_notes: Improved cross-SDK credential memoization and a slimmer streaming adapter - non-breaking. Suggest SDK version minor bumps for Go/Python/TS to pick up ergonomics and perf fixes.
description:
Summary: Add a focused credential memoization layer across SDKs and introduce a lightweight stream adapter that reduces allocation churn, improves backpressure signaling, and harmonizes retry hints between Python/TypeScript/Go. Motivation: We saw recurring hot-path overhead from credential lookups and excessive per-chunk allocations in high-throughput streaming customers (internal canary). This PR reduces token-path auth calls, provides a small in-memory memo for short-lived credentials, and replaces a heavyweight stream wrapper with a zero-copy-friendly adapter that surfaces retry/backoff hints to the transport layer.

Changes included (high level):
- New cross-language credential memoization module (ttl-based, fast-path lookup, opt-out). Implemented in core client layer and exposed as an optional config in each SDK.
- Lightweight StreamAdapter: a smaller internal abstraction that exposes explicit pause/resume hooks, consumer-visible ProgressHints, and a typed transient error wrapper used by retry policies.
- AdaptiveRetryAdapter: glues transport errors and ProgressHints into adaptive backoff selection (latency-aware).
- Minor ergonomic surface changes: clearer async generator docstrings/examples, a dedicated 'close_gracefully' helper, and improved type comments for TS/Go.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for TTL memo, integration tests for streaming resume, and a micro-benchmark showing ~22% reduction in per-request auth latency and ~15% lower allocations in stream-heavy scenarios.

Commits (summary):
- 9c2b1d3: Introduce cred memo interface + Python/TS/Go implementations and feature flags.
- 4f7e2a9: Replace StreamWrapper with StreamAdapter; wire ProgressHints into transport layer.
- a7d9c3b: Add AdaptiveRetryAdapter and update retry presets to consult ProgressHints.
- b1f0e5a: Docs examples, migration notes, and changelog entries; add unit + integration tests.

Files/areas touched (illustrative):
- sdk/core/auth/memo.go (Go) - TTL memo + lru-lite
- sdk/py/redwood/auth/memo.py - TTL memo + opt-out config
- sdk/ts/src/auth/credMemo.ts - lightweight memo implementation
- sdk/*/stream/adapter.* - new adapter implementations for each SDK
- sdk/*/retry/adaptive_adapter.* - adapter glue for retry selection
- docs/sdk/auth.md - new section describing memo tradeoffs and toggles
- examples/streaming/stream_retry_hints - updated example that uses close_gracefully and ProgressHints

Compatibility / migration notes:
- Default behavior remains unchanged for existing customers; memoization is enabled by default but limited to a conservative TTL (30s) and a small entry cap to avoid long-lived caching of rotated credentials. Ops teams can opt-out via client config or environment toggle.
- StreamAdapter is an internal refactor that preserves public async/iterator ergonomics; consumers using private internal wrapper types must update (rare). We added a compatibility shim for one release cycle.

Benchmarks & testing:
- Micro-bench harness under benchmark-lab shows median auth lookup reduced by 22% under our canary workload (many short-lived stream requests).
- Streaming allocation profiler demonstrates ~15% reduction in allocations per chunk with the new adapter in the Node runtime.
- CI ran full unit test matrix across py/ts/go, integration streaming tests in CI sandbox, and performance smoke tests in perf-canary. All checks passed on final run.

Review conversation (high level extract):
- Omar Li: "Nice, this addresses a clear hotspot we measured. Two asks: ensure TTL is configurable and add opt-out; and include a brief note for infra about potential KMS traffic changes."
- Nadia Park (author): "TTL is configurable via client opts (doc added). KMS traffic should be unchanged since we only short-circuit local credential lookups; added note to ops as requested."
- Priya Shah: "Can the ProgressHints be extended later to include percent-complete? I want to avoid API churn."
- Nadia Park: "We intentionally kept ProgressHints minimal (bytes/chunks/last-event) to avoid surface area growth; percent-complete can be added but will be additive-only and annotated in the doc. Added a unit test to ensure extension won't break adapters."
- Ethan Moore: "Small nit: rename close() -> close_gracefully() to signal flush semantics."
- Nadia Park: "Renamed and updated examples."

CI history: initial run flagged a flaky TS test (stream-chunk-order) — root cause: nondeterministic setImmediate ordering in our test harness. Fix committed in a7d9c3b and rerun. Final CI summary: all checks green (unit, lint, integration, perf-smoke).

Why this approach: The memoization solves frequent short-lived auth lookups (hosted auth rotations and delegated tokens) without introducing long-term caching risks. The StreamAdapter reduces allocation churn and gives the runtime explicit hints to make smarter retry/backoff choices under partial-progress conditions (e.g., intermittent network stalls). Keeping the change opt-out and conservative by default preserves safety for enterprise customers with strict key rotation rules.

Risk assessment: Low-medium. Main risk is mis-caching long-lived credentials; mitigations: small default TTL, explicit opt-out, and telemetry to surface unusual hit rates. We added a guardrail that emits a metric when an entry exceeds 5x the configured TTL.

Merge: Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-07 after approvals from Omar Li and Priya Shah.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4521: Add telemetry dashboards for memo hit/miss and oversized entries (next sprint).
- ENG-4598: Backfill minimal examples and bump SDK minor versions (py: 2.14.0 -> 2.15.0, ts: 1.28.0 -> 1.29.0, go: v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0).

Notes for release: include short doc blurb in the SDK changelogs and a compatibility note in the Private installer upgrade guide.
